order_dependence_by_block_dim.reading: the pn/np gap is carried ENTIRELY by the >=2-dim blocks; the 1-dim blocks are order-blind, which reconciles this probe with qou-99qc/#7295's altChar order-blindness result

one_sidedness.reading: MEASURED: mu depends only on the SECOND nucleon. The mechanism is NOT established -- sigma_3 lies inside block 1, but G^3 also carries sigma_2, adjacent to block 0's sigma_1, so far-commutation does not explain it.

the template bond is pair-INDEPENDENT, so it can never sign-mix
step-3's mu_pp(G^3) is reproduced to its quoted precision
mu_pp(G^3) > 1: the gamma-gamma bond DOES unbind the diproton
the gamma-gamma bond IS pair-dependent (it reaches into a nucleon block via sigma_3, so the bond-product theorem does not apply)
REPORTED, not required: whether G^3 makes 3He's b3 positive -- it is negative
REPORTED, not required: whether G^3 makes 3H's b3 positive -- it is negative

CROSS-ARC CONSISTENCY (qou-99qc / #7295): the 1-dimensional blocks contribute NOTHING to the pn/np gap -- a 1-dim rep is a product of scalars and is order-blind, so their order-blindness and this probe's order-DEPENDENCE are not in conflict
the whole pn/np gap is carried by the >=2-dimensional blocks
the two chains AGREE in sign under G^3 (a single bond family cannot give one atom a positive b3 and the other a negative one without that being a finding in itself)
